note:

item: אסי \- Possibly a variant of "Asa", meaning "physician" or "healer"
אשי / אשיאן / אשייאן / אשיין\- Jastrow believes is related to יאסין / יסיאן / יאסיין . It’s possibly a descendant of the name Yehoshua.
note:
OD \# 571-579.

Entry “ [אשיאן](sefaria:Jastrow,_אַשְׁיָאן.1)”: “\[see entry\] יאסין “.

Cf. the Christian name ישוע (Jesus), transcribed as Isho:   
[Isho'dnah \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isho%27dnah)  
[Ishodad of Merv \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishodad_of_Merv)  
[Ishoʿ of Merv \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isho%CA%BF_of_Merv)

OD \# 597-606. Variants:   
ביבא, ביבון  
Many commentators believe that this name is already found in the Bible, and is the same as the late Biblical name *“Bevai”,* in the books of Ezra and Nehemia. “[ביבי](sefaria:Jastrow,_בֵּיבַי.1)”. See also [רב ביבי – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%A8%D7%91_%D7%91%D7%99%D7%91%D7%99), footnote 1:   
“ השם בֵּבָי מצוי בתנ"ך (עזרא, ב', י"א ועוד), ויש מסורות שניקדו בהתאם את שם האמורא רב בֵּיבָי, על פי מסורת ניקוד אחרת שם האמורא מנוקד בֵּיבִי. ראו שרגא אברמסון, "לחקר הערוך", *לשוננו* לז (תשל"ג)”.  
Cf. the roughly contemporary Syriac Christian name “Babai” (spelled in Syriac Aramaic as ܒܵܒܲܝ \= בבי): [Babai the Great \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babai_the_Great) ; [Babai of Seleucia-Ctesiphon \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babai_of_Seleucia-Ctesiphon)

item: חנא \- Probably related to the Hebrew name "Chanan".
חנן \- Related to Hebrew name חנניה
טובי \- Related to Hebrew name טוביה.

note:
OD \# 2095-2099; 2124-2126. Variants:   
מנה, מני  
Cf. [Mani (prophet) \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_\(prophet\)): “Mani (\[...\] Syriac ܡܐܢܝ ܚܝܐ Mānī ḥayyā "Living Mani", circa CE 216/2 \- 274/277) \[...\] The exact meaning of the name is a question still unsolved. It may have derived from Babylonian-Aramaic Mânâ \[luminescence\]. Mandaeans used the term mânâ rabba, which means "Enlightened Lord/King".Ancient Greek interpretations were skeuos (σκεῦος, vessel, instrument) and homilia (ὁμιλία, intercourse, company, communion, instruction)  
The same slightly contemptuous "a certain" (Manes quidam) also appears in Hegemonius' Acta Archelai (4th century)”
OD \# 2152-2160 (the rest are honorific, and not given name: \#2161-2171).

OD \# 2231-2235. Variants:   
נהוריי.

Compare the Hebrew Mishnaic name מאיר, which means the same thing. The Talmud says that R’ Meir was also named Nehorai.

item: נחומי \- Diminutive of Hebrew name נחום
סימון \- from Hebrew name שמעון, as well as from an unrelated Greek etymology, “flat-nosed”
note:
OD \# 2369-2373.

[Simon (given name) \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_\(given_name\)): “Simon is a given name, from Hebrew \[Shimon\]. It is also a classical Greek name, deriving from an adjective meaning "flat-nosed". In the first century AD, Simon was the most popular male name for Jews in Roman Judea.” Citing Ilan, pp. 56–57; Hachili, pp. 113–115; Bauckham (2017), *Jesus and the Eyewitnesses*, p. 71: “15.6% of men bore one of the two most popular male names, Simon and Joseph.”

item: סמא / סימיי / סימאי\- Probably a diminutive of Simon

note:
OD \# 2408-2420. Variants:   
עולה  
Compare the Arabic name ʿUlā (على \- עלא). For example, [Hashim ibn Abd Manaf \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashim_ibn_Abd_Manaf): “born ʿAmr al-ʿUlā”.  
And the later name popular among Arabic-speaking Jews: ‘Ali \- עלי.

OD \# 2422-2433. Variants:   
עוקבן, עוקבה  
Cf. The Arabic name ʿUqba ) (= عقبة \- עקבה), popular in the early Muslim period (7th century):   
[Uqba ibn Amir \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uqba_ibn_Amir)  
[Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uqba_ibn_Abi_Mu%27ayt)  
[Uqba ibn Nafi \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uqba_ibn_Nafi)  
[Uqba ibn al-Hajjaj \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uqba_ibn_al-Hajjaj)  
[Uqba bin al-Harith \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uqba_bin_al-Harith)

OD \# 2452-2461. Variants:   
ענני  
Cf. [Anan (name) \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anan_%28name%29): “Anan (Hebrew: עָנַן ‘ānan) is used as both a Hebrew or Arabic name meaning "cloud, vapour" or descriptive "visible water vapour floating above the earth" \[...\] Notable people with the Hebrew name include:  
Anan, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Nehemiah 10:27)  
Anan (amora), Babylonian Jewish scholar  
Anan ben David, Karaite  
Saul ben Anan, Karaite Jewish leader of the eighth century CE”
OD \# 2518-2529. Cf. Tal Ilan who believes that the name Pappa is in fact Persian, not Aramaic.

item: רבה / רבא\- Contraction of רב אבא. Alternatively, related to Rabba, meaning “Great”
note:
OD \# 2581-2639.  
Shamma Friedman in an article in *Sinai* on the names רבא ורבה points out that in manuscripts of the Talmud, the two names are spelled the same.

item: רבינא \- Contractions of רב אבינא. Alternatively, related to “Great” \- רבא

note:
OD \# 2948-2961.  
ראו גם תלמידי ישו: [יעקב בן חלפי – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%99%D7%A2%D7%A7%D7%91_%D7%91%D7%9F_%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%A4%D7%99) (son of Alphaeus) ; [מתי – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%9E%D7%AA%D7%99) \- "מתי בן חלפי או לוי" .   
[Matthew the Apostle \- Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_the_Apostle):  
"In passages parallel to Matthew 9:9, both Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 describe Jesus's calling of the tax collector Levi, the son of Alphaeus".  
Compare the name “Ilfa” that appears in Talmud Bavli:   
[אילפא – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%A4%D7%90)  
And see Levin, “Midrashei”, p. 41, and bibliography there:   
“כאן מדרש שם כפול בשמו (שבתלמוד ירושלמי נקרא "חילפיי" או "אילפיי") כש"אילפא" פירושו "לימוד" וגם "ספינה". בזה מתחדד היחס והעימות המדומה בין לימודו ליציאתו למסחר (בספינה, כדרך התגרים, לרוב במקורות).   
See, also, variations of the name “Halfa” here:   
[אבא בר קורייה – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%90%D7%91%D7%90_%D7%91%D7%A8_%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%99%D7%94): "כיוון שהוא מובא בספרות חז"ל פעמים מעטות יש חילופים רבים בשמו. אבא- מובא גם כ"אבה". ברוב המקומות מובא עם שם שני, בחילופים רבים- "חלפוי", "חלפו", "חליפא", "חלפי", "חלפון", "חלבו"."  
Other names with the root חל”פ are likely cognate: חלפתא ; תחליפא. Cf.:   
[רבי חלפתא בן שאול – המכלול](https://www.hamichlol.org.il/%D7%A8%D7%91%D7%99_%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%A4%D7%AA%D7%90_%D7%91%D7%9F_%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%95%D7%9C)  
[רבה בר תחליפא – המכלול](https://www.hamichlol.org.il/%D7%A8%D7%91%D7%94_%D7%91%D7%A8_%D7%AA%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%A4%D7%90)  
[רב תחליפא בר אבדימי – ויקיפדיה](https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%A8%D7%91_%D7%AA%D7%97%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%A4%D7%90_%D7%91%D7%A8_%D7%90%D7%91%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%99)
